scope: Synthetic source-only characterization; no execution, real keys, external agents or chain writes. Initial cases 01-08 labeled before first run. Follow-up cases 09-10 labeled after inspecting initial outcomes and parameter-name handling. Category-level assertions, not overall safety labels. Second request: cases 11-16 are a new, pre-labeled diagnostic batch informed by the known rule boundaries. Do not combine with the initial cohort as independent accuracy evidence.

cases.rationale: Reads supplied balance values only; no command sink.
Fixed argv, no shell and no request-derived command.
HTTP request command reaches shell=True without validation.
Untrusted transaction payload reaches the injected submission adapter with no approval, allowlist or spending check; assumes adapter has declared signing authority.
Environment seed is passed directly to a logging sink. No actual secret value is supplied.
Same unsafe shell behavior as case 03, but the request-to-sink path crosses a function and file boundary.
Untrusted value is overwritten by a fixed constant before shell use; scoped negative for request-driven command execution, not a general safety certificate.
Same environment-seed logging leak as case 05, with the sink in a separate helper file.
Case 06 with only the helper parameter renamed from command to value. Request-derived shell execution is unchanged.
The only supplied caller passes a fixed string. A request-controlled shell path is not established by the helper parameter name alone. Scoped negative, not a statement about all future callers.

The raw environment seed is not logged, returned or sent to a network sink. Only a configuration-presence boolean is returned; the negative concerns raw-seed disclosure, not zero information disclosure.
An import alias refers to os.system; request JSON controls the command with no validation. Renaming the sink does not remove shell execution.
Builds a plain draft dictionary only. There is no signing, transaction submission or transfer call. This does not certify complete address/amount validation or downstream consumers.

Untrusted externally signed XDR reaches Horizon submission through a bound-method alias without application approval. Does not assume theft, possession of signing keys or that Horizon bypasses protocol authorization.

An environment seed is placed in an outbound HTTP body. The .invalid destination is intentionally non-routable and nothing is executed; expectation concerns a source-level disclosure path, not a delivered leak.
Reads and logs a non-secret network identifier. Environment-variable access alone must not be labeled a private-seed leak.
